title: I don’t find one single moment of AIRPLANE! Funny

commenti.body: [removed]
[removed]

Despite your stance on not enjoying set up comedy it seems, there are several jokes I would think you might still enjoy. All of Leslie Nielsen's banter is deadpan and the argument between the PA announcers at the beginning during their announcements is dark and builds organically as background noise.  Much of it is very broad but I would think that surely you'd be able to find a few jokes funny.
[removed]

You're talking about what I call the "organic" element of humor, where you have a real or at least reasonable set of circumstances and characters which are manipulated by the authors/performers to create a humorous response. That can be broad or dry, doesn't matter. The humor arises in a "natural" way from the situation & characters. You seem tom like that kind of humor. Good for you.

Airplane is more manipulative. Clever, word play, forced and absurd juxtaposition. You seem not to like that as much. Too bad, as that makes your life a little smaller. But everybody doesn't like everything and they don't arrest you for that. Move along.

Surely you can’t be serious?

But in all seriousness, it’s funny but I think it’s not the funniest movie ever like some people say. I like situational humor far more than Airplane’s gag humor. 

The Red Zone/White Zone part is about as funny as it gets though.
I'd be interested to see what other comedy you like. I feel like you'd enjoy the Marx Brothers, the dialogue is hilarious to me and there's some slapstick so maybe it's more up your alley.

There’s tons of word play on top of the sight gags. Most of those gags are very early on too. Feels like you saw 1 or 2 did the Leo point meme and checked out of the movie. As someone who listened to Harmontown through its entirety, I’d bet good money Dan loves Airplane.

It's certainly a matter of taste, but I'm not sure the Ace Ventura analogy holds up. 

The sight gag of "here's a guy in a silly outfit" can be a legitimate joke in principle, and it doesn't always require a lot of justification. A guy with a monocle is mildly funny, or at least silly. The unpardonable crime is that Jim Carrey tries to add a punch line by explaining the joke. And the explanation isn't even witty: most people could come up with "Monopoly Man" in real life, let alone in a writer's room. 

I can't think of anything like that in Airplane. In most cases the characters don't even react to the absurdity around them, let alone explain why it's absurd. When Nielsen answers the question "Surely you can't be serious?" with "Don't call me Shirley," nobody pipes up to mock him for his poor grasp of English.

Airplane! has aged really, really poorly.

It simply doesn't stand up to the test of time. You'll see a lot of push-back here from Boomers and older Gen Xers who likely have an emotional attachment to it for completely subjective reasons who also don't have the education to be able to separate their subjective love of a film from that film's objective quality.

It's archaic doo-doo. It's about as timeless as Tommy Boy or Half Baked. 

Don't know what those movies are? Exactly.

You’re trying to apply logic to a pure slapstick comedy.

It’s one long running gag with visual pieces to reinforce the jokes.

There’s nothing to actually “GET”. 

You don’t like that type of comedy, no biggie, just steer clear of Spaceballs entirely

Airplane! just isn't good. 

I am an Xennial so I'm old enough to be able to get some of the jokes and they still seem SO steeped in boring Boomer-specific stuff like the Vietnam War and Saturday Night Fever and sexual mores of the day.

I like dark, witty humor best - I lean towards British humor - but there are plenty of silly 80s comedies with Steve Martin or John Candy that I still enjoy and Airplane! is not on that list.
Airplane isn't as good as you think it is. The OPs life isn't "smaller" because of it.
